newsitem.title: UK: L&G leads insurers up as bid talk persists.
newsitem.headline: L&G leads insurers up as bid talk persists.

text.p: Legal and General Group Plc led UK insurance shares higher on Monday as bid speculation in the sector continued to simmer, fuelled by reports that Australia's AMP was planning to buy a sizeable UK life and pensions company.

By 1017 GMT Legal and General shares were nine pence higher at 388 on volume of 508,765 shares. Other life insurers also gained, with Prudential Corp Plc up four pence at 506-1/2 and Brittanic Assurance 20p higher at 762-1/2.
Among composites, Guardian Royal Exchange Plc climbed 4-1/2p to 269-1/2 and General Accident Pl rose 8-1/2p to 777.
"There have been speculative buyers in this sector for the last couple of weeks and they are in again this morning," one market-maker said.

A report in Monday's Financial Times quoted AMP's global merger and acquisition activity head, Jonathan Schwartz, as saying the company had about three billion pounds to spend on global expansion and Britain would be used as a platform to expand into Europe.
